The datasets that the `oceanbench` library uses are now described in the [OceanBench data catalog on EDITO](https://datalab.dive.edito.eu/data-catalog/data/catalogs/projects/oceanbench/oceanbench-catalog), that you can browse online.

## What you find

The catalog follows the [STAC](https://stacspec.org) specification and groups the datasets by origin: one collection per top-level directory of the OceanBench bucket, and one for Copernicus Marine.
It is rebuilt automatically from the bucket content and from the `oceanbench` source code.

Each dataset is described by an item with:

- its spatial and temporal extent, dimensions and variables, with CF standard names and units,
- Python examples to open it, with the [`oceanbench` datasets API](/documentation/api/index.qmd) or the Copernicus Marine Toolbox,
- the `oceanbench:library_usage` and `oceanbench:library_functions` properties, telling whether the `oceanbench` library uses it and which functions lead to it.

## Query it from Python

The catalog is also served by the EDITO STAC API, for example with [`pystac`](https://pystac.readthedocs.io):

``` python
import pystac

catalog = pystac.Catalog.from_file(
    "https://api.dive.edito.eu/data/catalogs/projects/oceanbench/oceanbench-catalog"
)
for collection in catalog.get_children():
    print(collection.id, collection.title)
```

The [data catalog documentation](/documentation/data-catalog/index.qmd) describes the collections and the programmatic access.
